factor_diagnostics.value_notes: Satellite-tag studies in the North Atlantic and Southwest Atlantic report blue marlin spending most tracked time in warm surface waters, commonly around 26–30 °C; the Southwest Atlantic study (21 fish) reports most time at 26–28 °C. factor_diagnostics.value_notes: Satellite-tag studies in the North Atlantic and Southwest Atlantic report blue marlin spending most tracked time in warm surface waters, commonly around 26–30 °C; the Southwest Atlantic study (21 fish) reports most time at 26–28 °C. These data support the broad 23–31 °C band and 26–29 °C ideal as a reasonable species-level habitat association, but population/region and tag-sample differences remain, and the studies do not establish a South Florida catch-probability curve.

factor_diagnostics.value_notes: Satellite tags show blue marlin primarily occupying the upper 100 m while making occasional dives to several hundred meters and, in some North Atlantic deployments, nearly 1,000 m. These are fish vertical dive depths, not bathymetric depths of the seafloor. The sources support pelagic water-column use but do not validate the configured 100–4,000 m bathymetric range or 200–2,000 m ideal. Depth remains an active gate.
